about: Example search queries for FLA-13 (docs/research/search.md) and the build task after it.
Each case has the query, what Octo does today, what Deezer's keyless track search returned when it was run for this research, and what a fixed search must do.

'deezer' was measured live on 2026-10-10 from one machine, one request per query (limit 25), so counts and order will drift. 'today' is traced from code, and the parts marked executed were run as unit-level code paths with stubbed upstream answers (see the doc). Nothing here records what Last.fm answers, because no API key was available.

scenarios.description: Any query with no Last.fm API key.
scenarios.today: ExternalSearchService.GetAsync returns no songs and makes no calls (executed). Search is the library only.

expect.note: With the fix on, songs still appear for an exact query such as 'Blinding Lights' without a Last.fm key.

scenarios.description: Library holds exactly one song that matches; query 'daft punk'.
scenarios.today: Library returns 1 row. Page one gives the 11 unused library slots back to discovery (executed: external rows on page one = 19 at songCount 20).

expect.note: Page one should show the library row first, then at least 15 outside rows.

cases.today: Sent to Last.fm verbatim as track.search. Result count equals what Last.fm returns (executed: Octo adds nothing and drops nothing). If it returns under 20 rows, a second call asks for the top tracks of an artist called 'Blinding Lights' (executed URL), which finds nothing.

songCount 5 is under the local floor of 12, so SearchBudget gives local=5, external=0 (executed). No outside call is made at all; the user sees library rows only.

expect.note: By design for per-keystroke type-ahead. The build task must keep external calls at zero here, or make a deliberate decision to change it (open question in docs/research/search.md).

cases.today: track.search first; under 20 rows triggers the pad with the first hit's artist (executed: 1 hit plus 40 top tracks gave 41 songs). Works when the artist is spelled right and Last.fm knows it.

Sent verbatim. The remix word is not understood as a version marker on the query side. Octo's dedupe keeps remixes apart (executed: 'dualipa|levitating|remix' differs from 'dualipa|levitating'), so Octo does not collapse them; fewer remixes come from the upstream's recall.
This is the example LastFmSearchCleanup was written for: Last.fm answers with mislabelled rows that the cleanup repairs. Versions stay separate rows after cleanup.

expect.note: Rows must not be listed under artist 'Kavinsky Nightcall' or '[unknown]'.
